Web design in Plano, TX has a pricing problem that has nothing to do with skill. A large share of the agencies working along the Dallas North Tollway and Legacy Drive build for companies with marketing departments, and their quotes are set for those buyers. If you run a two-person HVAC outfit off Parker Road, a nail studio in a strip center on Coit, or a family law practice near downtown, you are asking the same firms for something much smaller and getting a price built for something much bigger.

Dominion Web Design Pro is a small website builder in East Texas. Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand, shows you a free demo before any money changes hands, and charges one time: $497, $997 or $1,997. This page explains what a Plano small business actually needs online, and where we fit and do not fit.

Plano is a corporate city with a small business economy underneath it

Plano is home to about 290,000 people according to the Census Bureau's 2023 estimate, and it keeps attracting headquarters. In January 2026 AT&T announced it will build a 54-acre global headquarters campus at 5400 Legacy Drive, on the former EDS site, and pull its Dallas, Plano and Irving administrative offices into it, with partial move-in targeted as early as the second half of 2028. The city approved $20 million in incentives for the project in February 2026. That site had been planned as the Texas Research Quarter, a life sciences district, until AT&T's plans replaced it.

Every one of those corporate employees needs a dentist, a mechanic, a lawn crew, a dry cleaner and somewhere to eat lunch. That is the part of Plano this page is for: the independent businesses along US 75, Spring Creek Parkway, Park Boulevard and Preston Road that serve the people who work in the towers.

Why local search matters more as Plano gets better connected

In October 2025 DART opened the Silver Line, a 26-mile commuter rail line from Plano to DFW Airport, with Plano stations at 12th Street and Shiloh Road. The 12th Street station, one stop south of Downtown Plano, is also served by the Red Line and, at peak hours, the Orange Line. More ways in means more people passing through who did not grow up here and do not have a favorite plumber or a regular barber. When they need one, they search on a phone, and the businesses with a clear, fast website and a complete Google Business Profile get the call.

The same goes for new residents who move in for corporate jobs. They arrive without neighbors to ask. A website is often the first and only thing they check before they pick up the phone, so it needs to answer three questions in the first screen: what you do, which part of Plano and the surrounding suburbs you cover, and how to reach you right now.

What a Plano small business site should include

  • A plain statement of the service and the area, for example "Residential electrician serving Plano, Allen and Richardson."
  • One page per service, so a search for a specific job lands on the page that answers it.
  • Real photos of your work, your shop or your staff instead of stock pictures of handshakes.
  • A tap-to-call number at the top of every page and a contact form that has been tested.
  • Your hours, your map and your Google reviews where people can see them.
  • Page titles, descriptions and a sitemap set up so search engines can read the site properly.

The Plano businesses that gain the most

Home service trades get the clearest return, because plenty of Plano neighborhoods have been standing for decades and roofs, water heaters, fences and HVAC units wear out on a schedule. Owners search for those jobs by name. Independent medical, dental and counseling practices come next: their patients compare two or three offices on a phone before booking, and a thin site loses that comparison. Restaurants, tutoring centers, fitness studios and pet businesses round it out. None of these need a hundred pages. They need the right ten, written about the actual business.

Four reasons a Plano business would hire Dominion Web Design Pro

The price is not set against Legacy West rents

Our prices are printed on the site and they are the same for a Plano bakery as for a shop in Big Sandy. You are not paying toward a corporate-park office or a sales team.

The free demo is built for your business name and trade. If it does not look right for a Plano customer, you walk away owing nothing.

Pages are written for the suburbs you serve

Plano businesses usually work across Collin County and into Dallas. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each researched and written separately, so the Allen page does not read like the Richardson page with the name changed.

Help for Plano small businesses beyond the website

A website is one piece. Plano has good free help for the rest, and we would point you there before we sell you anything extra:

  • Collin SBDCThe Small Business Development Center run by Collin College with the U.S. Small Business Administration and the State of Texas offers free business counseling from the Courtyard Center at 4800 Preston Park Boulevard in Plano.
  • Plano Chamber of CommerceNetworking, ribbon cuttings and member events for local businesses across the city.
  • City of Plano Economic DevelopmentThe city department that works with employers moving to or expanding in Plano, worth knowing if you sell to them.

If the SBDC helps you write a business plan, bring it to us. It makes the services page and the about page much easier to write well.

Which package fits a Plano business

Starter, $497: five pages for a business that mostly needs to look real and be reachable, such as a single-location salon or a handyman covering a few zip codes in East Plano.

Pro, $997: ten pages with a gallery, local SEO setup including schema and your Google Business Profile, your Google reviews on the site, and ten city pages. This fits a home service company that drives to Allen, McKinney, Frisco, Richardson and Garland every week. The AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month if you keep it.

Agency, $1,997: keyword research first, then a hand-written page for every town and service pair the research says is worth having, usually 30 to 60 pages delivered in waves. Common questions

How much does web design cost in Plano, TX?

Agency quotes in Plano often start in the thousands because many firms here price for corporate clients. Dominion Web Design Pro charges $497 for a 5-page Starter site, $997 for the Pro package with 10 pages and 10 city pages, or $1,997 for the Agency package, all one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Do I need a web designer who is based in Plano?

Not for the website itself. The work is writing, design and setup, and all of it happens by link, phone and email. A Plano firm makes sense if you want someone in your conference room every month for brand workshops. If you mostly want a fast, honest site that explains your business, distance does not change the result.

Can my website show up for customers in West Plano, East Plano and nearby suburbs?

A site can be set up to say clearly where you work, with a service area page and, on the Pro package, ten city pages that each describe a nearby town such as Richardson, Allen, Frisco or Carrollton. Nobody can promise where Google places you. Reviews, your Google Business Profile and time all matter as much as the website.

Who owns the website and domain when it is finished?

You do. The domain is registered in your name, the pages and photos are yours, and if you ever move to a different company you take the whole site with you.

How fast can a Plano business get a new site live?

A Starter site goes live in 7 to 14 days once Maurice has your photos and details. The free demo comes first and costs nothing, so you can see the direction before you commit.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
